classification.difficultyReason: Track both jug volumes through successive transfers, recognising that the second fraction applies to the updated second-jug contents, then equate final volumes.

content.prompt: One jug has an unknown quantity of water. A second jug has 3 litres of water. One half of the contents of the first jug are transferred into the second jug, then one third of the contents of the second jug are transferred to the first jug. After which the two jugs contain the same amount of water. How much water was initially in the first jug?

answer.short:
3 litres.

Express each jug’s contents after both transfers and equate them.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ litres be the initial contents of the first jug. After the first transfer, the jugs contain $\frac{x}{2}$ and $3+\frac{x}{2}$ litres. After the second transfer, their contents are $\frac{x}{2}+\frac13(3+\frac{x}{2})$ and $\frac23(3+\frac{x}{2})$ litres.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{2}+\frac13\left(3+\frac{x}{2}\right)&=\frac23\left(3+\frac{x}{2}\right)\\3x+2\left(3+\frac{x}{2}\right)&=4\left(3+\frac{x}{2}\right)\\4x+6&=2x+12\\2x&=6\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
The first jug initially contained 3 litres.
